subject: Consumption corridor & smoothing reserve — commercial proposal

Subject: RFP follow-up — commercial clarification request

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the RFP response your team submitted last week. Procurement has one commercial question we need clarified before presenting to the finance committee:

1) Aurora will have bursty seasonal load (modeling window attached). We understand Redwood offers commits and overages — can you outline an approach that smooths our monthly invoice while keeping our committed spend footprint predictable? Specifically, we'd like to avoid large month-to-month volatility that triggers manual approvals.

2) What are the mechanics for discounts tied to multi-year commitments and how does early-exit / downgrade work?

3) Do you support a reserve/escrow mechanism to absorb short-term overages while leaving true-up annual? If so — what are the thresholds and pricing for that?

Appreciate a short commercial note and a worked example (numbers) we can show the committee.

Best,
Lena
Procurement Lead — Aurora Systems

Subject: RE: RFP follow-up — commercial clarification request

Hi Lena —

Thanks for the clear questions. I put together a short commercial proposal that maps to your ask and included a worked example using the usage window you shared. High level summary first, details below and in the attached PDF: redwood-consumption-corridor-pricing-v1.pdf.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Consumption corridor: a committed "corridor" (monthly baseline) + smoothing reserve (short-term buffer) to absorb bursts.
- Billing cadence: monthly invoices with a single annual true-up and carry-adjustment to preserve predictable monthly spend.
- Pricing: blended unit rates depending on committed corridor % of expected annual consumption; overage tiers inside smoothing reserve priced at a modest premium, over-escrow consumption at a higher overage rate.
- Multi-year discounts: front-loaded and step-down effective rates; early-exit has a 3-month exit premium on unused commit in first year only.

Worked example (based on your file):
- Aurora forecast (annual): 120B tokens (baseline).
- Proposed committed corridor: 6B tokens/month (72B annual) = 60% of forecast. Unit price inside corridor: $0.0008 / token.
- Smoothing reserve: 15% of monthly corridor (0.9B tokens) reserved to absorb bursts. Usage that falls into reserve is billed at $0.0010 / token (25% premium).
- Overflow (above corridor + reserve) billed at $0.0016 / token (100% premium).
- Monthly invoice smoothing: we bill corridor + consumed reserve; if reserve is used in a month we record a reserve draw. Annual true-up reconciles total consumed vs corridor purchased; any sustained excess converts to next-year commit crediting or invoice netting per the attached schedule.

Key mechanics and protections:
- Reserve re-fill: month-to-month, unused reserve capacity rolls forward for up to 2 months; reserves not used after 2 months expire (unless covered by a pre-agreed rollover).
- Cap on per-month volatility: automatic fallback to reserve for up to 50% of overage events before finance approval required.
- Invoice predictability: Redwood will send a pre-invoice forecast 5 days before month-end showing projected draw vs corridor and estimated invoice impact.

Multi-year discounting and early exit:
- 1-year: base rates as above.
- 2-year: 8% effective discount off blended unit price (applied across corridor).
- 3-year: 14% effective discount.
- Early-exit: if Aurora terminates in year 1, a 3-month equivalent of committed corridor (calculated at corridor unit rate) is due as an early-exit adjustment. Years 2+ have reduced exit charge (1 month).

Attachments included:
- redwood-consumption-corridor-pricing-v1.pdf (worked example and rate tables)
- usage-mapping-aurora.xlsx (annotated by Redwood)

I've CC'd Marissa (commercial lead) and Neha (pricing). If you'd like, Marissa can walk the committee through the worked example next Tuesday.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Commercial Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Consumption corridor & smoothing reserve — commercial proposal

Hi Lena —

Happy to present this to your committee. A few clarifying bullets from pricing ops that often get asked at committee time:

- Metering window: Redwood meters tokens at generation time; embeddings are accounted separately per line item (we can map your embeddings workload in the attached workbook).
- True-up options: annual default, optional semi-annual true-up at +0.5% admin fee.
- Overage escrow: we can establish an escrow buffer (pre-funded) equal to 10% of monthly corridor to guarantee immediate coverage for sustained surges; draws against escrow are invoiced monthly and reconciled at true-up.
- Audit & reporting: you’ll get token-level monthly CSV export and cost attribution by route/service.

If the committee prefers a higher predictability construct, two options are common:
1) Increase corridor to 80% of forecast (lower blended unit rate inside corridor).
2) Keep corridor at 60% and fund a larger smoothing reserve (25% of corridor) — this raises the blended cost modestly but reduces overage risk.

We can include a short slide for the committee showing the three scenarios and expected monthly invoice bands. Rafael / Neha — can you add scenario pricing to tab "CommitteeScenarios" in the workbook?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael / Marissa —

Committee liked the smoothing reserve concept. A couple of follow-ups before we escalate to legal:

1) Can Redwood provide a worked invoice example showing month-by-month billing for a 12-month period under scenario B (60% corridor + 15% reserve)? We want to show finance the likely invoice swing and reserve draw cadence.
2) On escrow: will Redwood accept an ACH pre-fund that Redwood draws from (we'd like the draw rules codified)? What are the refund rules if escrow is unused at year-end?
3) Any minimum seat/license or per-model surcharge we should be aware of for enterprise features (private deployment connectors, dedicated pools)?

If you can send the month-by-month example and proposed escrow draw/refund language, we can route to legal and get an LOI.

Best,
Jared Cole
Director, Cloud Procurement — Aurora Systems
